# Samathakkhandhaka (Kd 14)

**ID:** Kd 14
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Samathakkhandhaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14, comprising chapter IV of the *Cullavagga*) provides an extensive exposition of the procedures for resolving monastic legal issues (*adhikaraṇa*) [von Hinüber 1996; Prebish 1994]. It articulates how the seven rules for settling legal disputes (*adhikaraṇasamathadhamma*) found at the end of the Pātimokkha are implemented in monastic practice, and provides a technical analysis of the four classes of legal issues (*vivādādhikaraṇa*, *anuvādādhikaraṇa*, *āpattādhikaraṇa*, and *kiccādhikaraṇa*) [Vinayamukha 1983; Prebish 1994]. Scholars have highlighted its internal structural format, noting the presence of an early *mātṛkā* style that organizes disputes into categories such as right, wrong, and undetermined [Sung 1999]. In terms of relative chronology, Oskar von Hinüber notes that the text is familiar with the *Suttavibhaṅga* [von Hinüber 1996].

Substantively, the text details various formal ecclesiastical acts (*kamma*) and settlement mechanisms. These include the verdict in the presence of the assembly and the Dhamma (*sammukhavinaya*), the verdict of innocence based on recollection (*smṛtivinaya*), the verdict regarding an unrepented offense (*tassapāpiyasikākamma*), settlement through collective confession as if "covering with grass" (*tiṇavatthāraka*), and resolution upon acknowledgment (*pratijñākāraka*) [Vinayamukha 1983; Prebish 1994; Prebish 1996].

Full cross-sectarian parallels exist across monastic traditions, notably the *Adhikaraṇavastu* (or *Śamathavastu*) preserved in Sanskrit fragments and Tibetan translation, as well as Chinese Vinaya versions across the Mūlasarvāstivāda, Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka lineages [Härtel 1956; Banerjee 1979; Prebish 1994]. Sutta-level parallels treating the same settlement principles include the *Sāmagāma Sutta* (MN 104) and the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33) [Prebish 1996].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: san-mu-kd16 Adhikaraṇavastu; xct-mu-kd16 Samatha; lzh-mu-kd16 Samatha; Lzh Sarv Kd15 Samatha Khandhaka; Lzh Dg Kd 16 Samatha Khandhaka; Lzh Mi Kd 9 Samatha Khandhaka
- Passage-level parallels: AN 10.33 Ubbāhikāsutta; AN 6.36 Vivādamūlasutta; T 1536.7 六法品; DN 33 (PTS DN iii 207) Saṅgīti Sutta; MN 104 (PTS MN ii 243) Sāmagāma Sutta; AN 8.90 Sammāvattanasutta; Bu-Vb Ss8 Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 8
- Mentioned in: Pvr 7 Ekuttarikanaya; Pvr 4 Antarapeyyāla; Pvr 11 Adhikaraṇabheda; Pvr 5 Samathabheda

**Sources**

- [von Hinüber 1996] Oskar von Hinüber, A Handbook of Pāli Literature (1996) — Noted the alternative title Adhikaraņasamathakkhandhaka and its developmental relation to the Suttavibhaṅga.
- [Prebish 1994] Charles S. Prebish, Survey of Vinaya Literature (1994) — Detailed the specific procedures of the adhikaraṇa-śamatha-dharmas and Sanskrit vastu correlations.
- [Prebish 1996] Charles S. Prebish, Buddhist Monastic Discipline (1996) — Described specific rules such as covering with grass and pratijñākāraka, citing parallel explanations in MN 104.
- [Vinayamukha 1983] Somdet Phra Mahā Samaṇa Chao Krom Phraya Vajirañāṇavarorasa, The Entrance to the Vinaya (Vinayamukha), Vol. 3 (1983) — Detailed legal topics and kammavācā procedures in the chapter, including vivādādhikaraṇa, tiṇavatthāraka, and tassa-pāpiyasikākamma.
- [Sung 1999] Kang-yuan Sung, Tradition and Development in the Mo-ho-seng-ch'i-lu (1999) — Discussed the mātṛkā style recognized in the text by Rhys Davids and Oldenberg.
- [Härtel 1956] Herbert Härtel, Karmavācanā (1956) — Noted Turfan Sanskrit fragments corresponding to the Adhikaraṇa-Vastu and Cullavagga IV.
- [Banerjee 1979] Anukul Chandra Banerjee, Sarvāstivāda Literature (1979) — Observed the agreement between the Tibetan Vinayavastu and the Pali Samathakkhandhaka regarding dispute settlement.
